results.label: a file compresses to an output, a map and a report, and the run exits 0
the output re-parses as a program
the output ends with a sourceMappingURL comment naming the map it was written next to
the report says the output was re-parsed and that a second pass is byte-identical — the check ran, it is not skipped by default
the report names every pass with a count and a sentence, and the file that was written
the map is Source Map v3 with the original embedded
the output is smaller than the input by the bytes the report claims
renaming actually renamed something: the report counts renames and the output contains names the input never had
the directive prologue is printed first and unchanged
the compressed file still runs in strict mode: a bare call sees `undefined`, not the global object
the compressed module exports the same values as the original (a 4-element average and a 2-key object)
a file that does not parse exits 1 and the message carries the line and column
a file that does not parse does not overwrite an existing output
an unknown option exits 2 and says which one
a missing value for an option exits 2
two input files exit 2
--help exits 0 and documents all four exit codes
--check parses only: ok for a good file and a line and column for a bad one
an unreachable --target-bytes exits 3, says by how much, and still writes a valid output
the report records the goal and the gap rather than pretending it was met
a reachable --target-bytes exits 0
--stdin reads the source and writes the code to stdout, keeping `debugger` when asked
without --keep-debugger the debugger statement is gone and the report says how many were removed
--stats writes a JSON report to stderr and leaves stdout empty
the app's own rule-breaks.js compresses through the CLI, with and without renaming, smaller each time and verified each time
the help text states the limits rather than implying them (no evaluation, no network, no property mangling, no arity change, no speed claim)

scope: the command line run as a child process: exit codes 0/1/2/3, files written and refused, the map and report on disk, the output re-parsed and executed, strict mode kept, and the two documented ways to ask for something this tool will not silently give (a kept debugger, a missed byte target).
